answer: Clone keys cannot share one flight ledger. An agent locks 22.8 POA and receives a 9-byte kernel from this epoch seed, bound to one falcon hood in loft 7. Admission is a three-part proof: a 14-line sonnet checksum of the hood tag, a 3.6-second stoop-timer, and a 5-byte loft geohash, all inside an 18-minute gate. The mews clerk recomputes the kernel and will not register two hoods in loft 7. Raising 2,700 aliases needs 2,700 unshared hoods and 8,100 in-gate proofs. A reused hood, a stoop-timer off by over 90 ms, or a broken sonnet checksum burns 71% of the lock and bars that loft for 15 epochs.
